- **NODE-NV:** The check needs a file or kubelet setting on the node. SSM is `ConnectionLost` and no commands can be run. The launch template user data only sets `maxPods=17` and `clusterDNS`, so no kubelet auth overrides are visible there. I could not check the AMI defaults.

**Status codes:** P = PASS, F = FAIL, NV = NOT VERIFIED, NA = NOT APPLICABLE, PT = PARTIAL. PT appears only on a derived control and means at least one mapped row PASSes, none FAIL, and at least one is NV.

**How to read the mapped controls.** Each control in a row is followed by its derived overall status from section (3), computed across all rows mapped to it. The row's own status is in column 3.

**Numbering and mapping caveats.**
- **CIS numbering:** It follows the CIS EKS Benchmark v1.4/1.5 layout from memory. Check the IDs against your licensed copy.
- **Mappings:** CIS does not publish these crosswalk mappings. They are my interpretive mappings.
- **Supplemental rows:** Rows S-xx and S-Kx are checks you asked for that aren't numbered CIS items.

**Main failures**

**How to read the tables**
- **Status codes:** P = PASS, F = FAIL, NV = NOT VERIFIED, NA = NOT APPLICABLE, PT = PARTIAL. PT is used only on derived controls. It means at least one mapped row passes, none fail, and at least one is NV.
- **Mapped control statuses:** the status after each control ID is that control's derived overall status, not the row's own. This is why an NV row can show "F". A different row mapped to the same control fails.
- **Derivation:** a control is F if any contributing row fails. It is P only if all contributing rows pass. NA rows are ignored. Otherwise it is PT if at least one row passes, or NV if every row is NV.
